causes.label: network_outage
causes.quote: From 14 to 24 April, a planned outage of the Armidale - Sapphire line south of QNI (Diagram 1) created a credible risk that Queensland could be synchronously separated from the NEM.

causes.label: battery_state_of_charge
causes.quote: Neoen's Western Downs Battery offered 122 MW of low-priced L1 sec capacity for 5.30 pm but it could not be enabled to provide this as it was dispatching 255.57 MW into the energy market.

causes.label: rebids
causes.quote: Between 2.58 pm and 5.23 pm, AGL Energy moved a net total of 23 MW at its Wandoan Battery from low-price to $15,800 per MW.

interconnectors_named.name: QNI
interconnectors_named.quote: Queensland is connected by two interconnectors, QNI and Terranora. Of these, only QNI can transfer FCAS.

intervals.quote: In Queensland, the L1 sec price reached $2,634 per MW for the 30-minute period ending 5.30 pm on 20 April.

network_outages.quote: From 14 to 24 April, a planned outage of the Armidale - Sapphire line south of QNI (Diagram 1) created a credible risk that Queensland could be synchronously separated from the NEM.

peak_price.quote: In Queensland, the L1 sec price reached $2,634 per MW for the 30-minute period ending 5.30 pm on 20 April.

rebid_set_price.quote: This high-priced capacity was ultimately needed to meet the last 23 MW required for the 5.30 pm dispatch interval, which meant this unit set the price for this interval.

causes.label: interconnector_limit
causes.quote: At 6.55 pm on this day, the metered flow on Basslink was 0 MW. This meant Basslink was in its "No-Go" zone and unable to transfer FCAS.

causes.label: fcas_co_optimisation
causes.quote: On this occasion at 6.55 pm, AEMO's dispatch engine determined the cheapest outcome was to back off an offer of around -$1,000 per MWh from Hydro Tasmania's Liapootah, Catagunya, Wayatinah in energy, to provide more in raise services.

constraints_named.quote: Hydro Tasmania's load unit that only provides ancillary services was restricted during the high-priced interval under the Adaptive Under Frequency Load Shedding (AUFLS) scheme.

interconnectors_named.name: Basslink
interconnectors_named.quote: At 6.55 pm on this day, the metered flow on Basslink was 0 MW. This meant Basslink was in its "No-Go" zone and unable to transfer FCAS.

intervals.quote: The local Raise 6 second (R6 sec) 30-minute price in Tasmania was $834 per MW at 7 pm, which was the highest 30-minute price in the month.

peak_price.quote: The local Raise 6 second (R6 sec) 30-minute price in Tasmania was $834 per MW at 7 pm, which was the highest 30-minute price in the month.

rebid_set_price.quote: There were no significant rebids in R6 sec service for this event.

causes.label: fcas_co_optimisation
causes.quote: The main drivers were the trade-off between energy and FCAS markets, system normal constraints including an emergency frequency control scheme, Basslink in the "No-Go" zone and one minor rebid.

causes.label: network_outage
causes.quote: system normal constraints invoked by AEMO to maintain system security caused the local FCAS requirement in Tasmania to reach up to 66 MW at 6 pm.

causes.label: rebids
causes.quote: VIOTAS Australia removed 1 MW of low-priced capacity from its demand response unit, DRVIOT05, in a late rebid at 5.53 pm due to a change in plant conditions.

constraints_named.quote: the AUFLS control scheme (Box 4) was in place at the time and restricted Hydro Tasmania's load unit during the high-priced intervals.

interconnectors_named.name: Basslink
interconnectors_named.quote: From 9.35 pm, Basslink was in the "No-Go" zone (Box 3) and Tasmania had to provide its own local FCAS.

intervals.quote: In Tasmania, 30-minute prices were above $3,500 per MWh in energy and above $3,500 per MW in FCAS. The affected FCAS markets were Raise Regulation (RReg) and Raise 60 second (R60 sec) at 6 pm and R6 sec at 10 pm.

network_outages.quote: system normal constraints invoked by AEMO to maintain system security caused the local FCAS requirement in Tasmania to reach up to 66 MW at 6 pm.

peak_price.quote: Each 30-minute price was driven by a single 5-minute price spike at or near the market price cap (Table 2).

rebid_set_price.quote: This rebid contributed to the high price in R60 sec at 6 pm as only 1 MW of high-priced capacity was needed to meet the R60 sec requirement. DRVIOT05 also set the high price at the time.

causes.label: demand
causes.quote: South Australia experienced colder temperatures ranging from 4°C to 15°C on 21 and 22 June, resulting in higher than usual electricity demand.

causes.label: wind_output
causes.quote: South Australia experienced a wind lull on 21 and 22 June, with wind output averaging 85 MW out of 2,766 MW of registered wind capacity.

causes.label: battery_state_of_charge
causes.quote: batteries removed capacity in the lead up to the high prices as they ran out of charge

causes.label: interconnector_limit
causes.quote: South Australia had limited access to imports during the high-priced periods due to system normal constraints affecting both interconnectors.

causes.label: rebids
causes.quote: Rebidding for commercial and technical reasons contributed to some high prices on 21 and 22 June.

interconnectors_named.name: Heywood
interconnectors_named.quote: Heywood imports into South Australia were restricted, while Murraylink flows were forced counter-price (i.e. when high-priced generation in one region is forced into a region with lower-priced generation) into Victoria.

interconnectors_named.name: Murraylink
interconnectors_named.quote: Heywood imports into South Australia were restricted, while Murraylink flows were forced counter-price (i.e. when high-priced generation in one region is forced into a region with lower-priced generation) into Victoria.

intervals.quote: Across 21 and 22 June, the 30-minute price for energy exceeded $3,000 per MWh on five occasions. The 30-minute prices ranged from $3,836 per MWh to $20,300 per MWh (Table 8).
